headline: Cell-type-resolved mapping of genetic variant effects on brain gene expression
label: Cell Type Regulatory Variant Mapping
summary: Donor-scale single-cell and long-read sequencing now localizes genetic variant effects on expression to specific brain cell populations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is attributing genetic effects to defined cellular populations rather than bulk tissue. A preprint pairs long-read whole-genome sequencing of 100 Parkinson's brain samples, yielding 74,552 structural variants, with single-nucleus RNA-seq to link them to cell-type-specific expression effects. A published study maps QTLs for transcriptional noise in iPSC-derived midbrain scRNA-seq from 155 individuals and relates them to schizophrenia GWAS signals. The autism study on rare-variant gene-pair co-occurrence in cytoskeletal pathways does not share this thread, since its summary reports no cell-type resolution. What is new is the combination of cell-type identity, donor-scale cohorts, and variant-level annotation to localize genetic effects to particular cells.
